title: Waste oil, absorbents and environmental controls
audience: Cleaners and supervisors handling waste oil, contaminated absorbents and rags from industrial degreasing.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish approved waste containers and authorised handlers from unverified oils and absorbents.
Stop where a waste container has no label or approved collection path.
Record the concern and refer waste decisions to the competent person.

instruction.heading: What counts as waste in a degreasing job
instruction.body: Degreasing produces several kinds of waste. There is spent degreaser, rinse water that has picked up oil or solvent, rags and wipes soaked with product, absorbents laid down under spills, waste oil drained from machines, sludge from tanks, and empty containers that still hold residue. Each of these can carry hazards of its own, such as flammability, toxicity or environmental harm, and the risk depends on what it has been mixed with. The classification and disposal route are decided by the competent person and the lawful waste contractor, not by the cleaner. Your job is to recognise that a material is waste, keep it in the right container, label it accurately as the site requires, and refer any question about what it is or where it goes. The Safe Work Australia code on hazardous chemicals says that containers holding waste, and decanted containers, must be correctly labelled, and that chemicals of unknown content must be disposed of under the local waste requirements. That is a point of law for the site to confirm, not something a cleaner decides on the spot.

instruction.heading: Containers, labels and storage
instruction.body: A waste container should have a lid that closes, be made of a material that suits the content, and carry a label that says what is inside and what hazard it presents, in the form the site requires. Keep containers closed when they are not being filled. Store them where they cannot be knocked over, where spills can be contained, and away from ignition sources, heat and drains. Keep incompatible materials apart, so that a container of oxidising material is not stored with a flammable one, and do not place chemicals where they could contaminate food or personal items. The Safe Work Australia code also advises keeping chemicals clear of incompatible materials, including when stacking them. Historical Victorian guidance from 2009 described bulk tanks or 200 litre drums in an enclosed, bunded area, preferably under cover, or on spill containment pallets.

instruction.heading: Waste oil and oily absorbents
instruction.body: Waste oil and oily absorbents need special care. Used engine oil, gear oil and similar fluids are waste that must not be poured down a drain, put onto soil or burnt in an unlicensed fire. The 2009 Victorian guidance for motor and degreasing workshops said that oily rags, sand and sawdust contaminated with oil or solvent should be stored in a separate bin until a suitable disposal route is found, and that used oil filters should be recycled rather than sent to landfill. Current EPA Victoria guidance on transporting hazardous waste (updated 14 May 2025) does not name waste oil, so it does not settle the question either. The practical rule for a cleaner is firm. Keep oily rags out of ordinary bins, keep waste oil in its approved container, and refer the choice of route to the competent person.

instruction.heading: Environmental controls and spills
instruction.body: In Victoria, the EPA's general environmental duty (updated 4 August 2026) asks businesses to deal with the risk of harm from their waste or pollution, removing what can be removed and reducing the rest, to the extent that is reasonably practicable. That applies to waste oil and absorbents as much as to any other waste. In practice, keep waste sealed and within the approved area, keep spills off the ground and out of drains and stormwater, and use the approved absorbent to contain a spill. Do not hose an oil spill toward a drain, and do not use a drain as a way out of a spill. Stop the source where it is safe to do so, keep people clear, and report the spill immediately to the supervisor. Record what was spilled, roughly how much, where it went, and what was done.

instruction.heading: Stop, record and refer
instruction.body: Stop where a container has no label, where the content is not known, where the collection path is not approved, or where a container is in poor condition or leaking. Do not add material to the container, do not move it, and do not decide where it goes. Keep people away from the container where that is safe. Record the location, the label status, the lid condition, the visible condition, the source of what you know, the people informed and the restriction you put in place. State what is unknown, rather than guessing. Refer the matter to the supervisor, who should assign the competent person and the lawful waste contractor. Do not sign off a disposal route yourself, and do not accept a verbal assurance from another contractor that the material is fine to remove.

instruction.heading: Transport and handover of waste
instruction.body: Waste leaves a site with a carrier, and the carrier must be authorised for the waste type. Current EPA Victoria guidance on transporting hazardous waste (updated 14 May 2025) sets out the same general duty for carriers, asks that drivers complete waste-handling training, and notes that certain priority waste has to be tracked online in the EPA's Waste Tracker and covered by a permission. The site receiving the waste must also be authorised to take it. A cleaner should not load, carry or transport waste unless the site and the carrier have confirmed in writing that the cleaner is authorised to do so and the training and permissions are in place. This lesson does not grant any transport or disposal authority.

procedure: Before adding material to any waste container, check that it is labelled, that the content is known, and that the collection path is approved.
If the label, the content or the path is missing, stop. Do not add to the container or move it.
Keep waste oil and oily absorbents out of drains, stormwater and the ground, and keep oily rags in their own closed container.
Use the approved absorbent to contain a spill, keep people clear, stop the source if safe, and report the spill immediately.
Keep containers closed, stored apart from incompatible materials, and away from drains and ignition sources.
Record the location, label status, lid condition, source of information, people informed and restriction applied.
Refer the waste decision to the supervisor, who assigns the competent person and the lawful waste contractor, and do not sign off a disposal route yourself.

workedExamples.situation: A bin of solvent-contaminated rags has no waste label and no approved collection path. A colleague says to put your rags in it because the bin is nearly empty. (Example scenario.)
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop. Do not add your rags to the bin, and do not move it. Keep people away from the bin where that is safe, and record its location, the missing label, the lid condition and the colleague's suggestion as an unverified suggestion. Tell the supervisor, who should assign the competent person and the lawful waste contractor. Your rags go into a separate container once the approved route is confirmed.

workedExamples.situation: A hose connection leaks oil onto the yard near a stormwater grate during a degreasing job. (Example scenario; the yard and quantities are fictional.)
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first sequence of actions?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the source if it is safe to do so, and keep people clear. Contain the spill with the approved absorbent, and do not hose it. Report it to the supervisor immediately, and, if trained and the site procedure allows, place the approved material to keep the oil away from the grate. Record what was spilled, roughly how much, where it went and what was done. The clean-up waste is then handled as waste under the same stop-record-refer routine.

workedExamples.situation: Several drums stand in an open yard with their lids missing, and rain is forecast. The drums are labelled, but the labels are faded and a supervisor is not on site. (Example scenario.)
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you move the drums or re-label them?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not move, re-label, open or add to the drums. Record the location, the lid status, the faded labels and the forecast, and keep people clear where that is safe. Refer the matter at once to the supervisor and the competent person, because the storage condition is a question for them. Any covering or relocation should be decided by them, under the site's storage procedure.

equipmentAndPpe: Approved absorbent and a spill kit held by the site, used only where trained.
Labelled, closable waste containers, one for each stream, including a separate container for oily rags.
Gloves suitable for oil and solvent as named on the SDS for each product.
Eye protection, and face protection where splashing is possible, as set by the SDS.
Closed footwear and clothing as the site procedure requires.
Spill and waste record form with space for location, label status and people informed.
Location of the nearest fire extinguisher and the site emergency contact.

commonErrors.error: Adding material to a container with no label or no approved path.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the label, the content and the path first. If any is missing, stop.

commonErrors.error: Hosing an oil spill toward a drain or stormwater grate.
commonErrors.prevention: Contain the spill with the approved absorbent, keep the grate clear, and report at once.
Refer route decisions to the competent person and the lawful waste contractor.

commonErrors.error: Putting oily rags into an ordinary bin.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the separate, closed container for oily rags, and refer its disposal.

commonErrors.error: Mixing incompatible wastes or storing them together.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep materials apart as the SDS and site procedure require, and check before adding anything.

commonErrors.error: Relying on a 2009 guide as the current requirement.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat older guidance as an example only, and confirm current requirements with the regulator and the site.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Under the EPA Victoria general environmental duty (updated 4 August 2026), businesses must remove or reduce the risks of harm from their waste or pollution so far as is reasonably practicable. This applies to waste oil and contaminated absorbents at Victorian sites.

The EPA Victoria page on transporting hazardous waste (updated 14 May 2025) applies the general duty to carriers, expects driver training, and calls for some reportable priority waste to be logged and permitted. The receiving site must be authorised to take it. This lesson does not grant any transport permit, permission or authority.

The Safe Work Australia hazardous chemicals code (July 2012 as shown) requires correct labelling of waste containers and decanted containers, separate storage from incompatible materials, and disposal under local waste requirements for chemicals of unknown content.

Historical Victorian guidance (dated June 2009) described storage of waste oil in enclosed, bunded areas, prohibited drain, soil and unlicensed burning disposal, and described oily rags as prescribed industrial waste. It describes an earlier framework.
Waste oil and absorbents must be classified, stored, transported and disposed of under the rules that apply where the work is done.

qualityStandard: Unlabelled container identified as a stop in the case study, with the cleaner not adding to it or moving it.
Spill containment described with the approved absorbent, with no hosing toward a drain, in the scenario.
Record completed with location, label status, condition, source, people informed and the restriction, and with the referral to the competent person.
No disposal route decided or signed off by the cleaner in any exercise.
documentationEvidence: Waste location and condition record, with label status and lid condition.
Spill record showing the material, approximate quantity, location, containment and people informed.
Referral record naming the competent person and the lawful waste contractor, and the decision pending.
summary: An unlabelled container with no approved path is a stop: do not add to it or move it.
Keep waste oil and oily absorbents out of drains, stormwater and the ground, and contain spills with the approved absorbent.
Record, restrict and refer; the competent person and the lawful waste contractor decide the route.

knowledgeChecks.question: A bin of solvent rags has no label or approved path. What is correct?
options: Stop, do not move it, and refer to the competent person
Add your rags to it, since it is already in use for the job
Move it to the skip, since it looks ready for disposal

knowledgeChecks.question: Where must waste oil never go?
Who decides the disposal route for waste oil?
options: The cleaner, once the bin is full and needs emptying
Anyone on the site who has time to sort it out
The competent person and the lawful waste contractor
